subject: ventures/bonus-take-home-gross-up-calculator
professional: a payroll specialist (CPP) who runs off-cycle bonus and gross-up payrolls. First checks: the supplemental-wage method in IRS Pub 15 section 7 (optional 22% flat, mandatory 37% on supplemental wages over $1,000,000 in the year), Social Security stopping at the year's wage base, employer withholding of the 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax only on wages over $200,000, 401(k) deferrals excluded from income-tax withholding but not FICA, employer match on SS and Medicare but not Additional Medicare, and a gross-up that solves net/(1 - sum of rates) and stays right across the caps.

evidence.correctness: Independent Python from Pub 15 / SSA 2026 figures (python3 /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/4c488086-781e-5ba3-9f2e-f786d86a9ac5/scratchpad/bonus/indep.py) against the engine (node /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/4c488086-781e-5ba3-9f2e-f786d86a9ac5/scratchpad/bonus/tool.mjs). Default example ($10,000 bonus, $90,000 YTD, 22% fed, 5% state): SS 620, Medicare 145, fed 2,200, state 500, net 6,535, settlement -200 at a 24% bracket, employer cost 10,765 -- identical. Gross-up of $10,000 net: closed form 10000/(1-.22-.05-.062-.0145) = 15,302.22, engine 15,302.22. Across the SS cap (YTD 180,000, 2026 base 184,500): closed form (10000 + .062x4500)/(1-.22-.05-.0145) = 14,366.18, engine 14,366.18. YTD 195,000: SS 0, Additional Medicare 45, employer cost 10,145 (no match on Additional Medicare) -- identical. FAIL: a $1,500,000 bonus at the labelled '22 is the flat supplemental rate' withholds 330,000 federal; Pub 15 section 7 makes 37% mandatory on supplemental wages over $1M, so 220,000 + 185,000 = 405,000, and the tool overstates take-home by $75,000; the gross-up for $1M net at YTD 200,000 of regular wages is 1,415,428 vs 1,527,403.41 under the mandatory rate (850,000 / 0.5565; corrected by the round lead from the auditor's 1,581,312, which holds only if the 200,000 was itself supplemental pay). FAIL: grossUp returns 6.43e64 when k401Pct=100 or the withholding rates sum to 100% (no solution exists), with no message. Typical-bonus arithmetic is exact; the missing mandatory-rate rule and the degenerate gross-up hold this at 2.
evidence.completeness: Claimed features checked by run: per-tax breakdown (works), SS wage-base cap (works), Additional Medicare over threshold (works), refund/balance due vs bracket (works), 401(k) deferral table (works; FICA kept on deferral), employer cost (works), exact gross-up (works on normal inputs; degenerate inputs not handled), size table (works). No stubs or TODOs. Single page only; llms.txt lists just the tool.
evidence.verification: cd ventures/bonus-take-home-gross-up-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs': 25/25 pass, 0.11 s. Tests use hand-checkable values (6,535; 279 at the cap; 45 Additional Medicare) and check the gross-up against the forward calculation. Five seeded mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py on calc.mjs: SS room ignoring YTD caught; state dropped from settlement caught; employer matching Additional Medicare caught; Additional Medicare threshold ignoring YTD caught; Additional Medicare dropped from afterTaxValue SURVIVED. 4 of 5 caught. No test covers bonuses over $1M or a gross-up with no solution.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (117 lines), index.html script (lines 133-164), usage.mjs, both test files. Engine is pure and small. Defects: index.html:138 opts() silently replaces any blank or unparsable field with its DEFAULTS value and rewrites the box, so a user who clears 'Wages already paid' to mean zero is computed at $90,000 and a cleared state rate becomes 5%; negative rates are silently clipped to 0 by nz(); grossUp's comment (calc.mjs:80-81) asserts net rises with gross 'everywhere', which is false at 100% deferral or rates summing to 100%, and the loop then returns 6.4e64 instead of failing; money()'s regex for '∞' hints the author saw Infinity but did not guard it.
evidence.claims: Checked: FAQ '22% + 5% state is about 35 cents of every dollar' = 34.65% (pass); 'a 401(k) deferral takes income tax off but not Social Security or Medicare' matches Pub 15 (pass); 'employer total cost with its matching Social Security and Medicare' excludes Additional Medicare correctly (pass); disclaimer, privacy line and 'Not decided' limits present (pass); usage events named on page match record() calls (page.test, pass); served llms.txt clean (node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs, the github.io link in source is rewritten). FAIL: meta description and the federal field label (index.html:7, :72) present 22% as 'the flat supplemental rate' with no mention of the mandatory 37% over $1M, and the 'Not decided' list omits it too. PARTIAL: README:25 'solved exactly (bisection on a monotonic net function)' is not true for every accepted input.
evidence.fitness: Walked the two jobs. An employee checking a $5k-$50k bonus gets each withheld line, the refund-or-owe estimate and the 401(k) effect: done. A small-business owner promising a $10,000 net sign-on gets 15,302.22 gross and 16,472.84 employer cost: done, matching a manual gross-up. Both jobs require the user to look up their own state supplemental rate (no state table; e.g. states with a fixed supplemental rate vs those using aggregate) -- disclosed. Executive bonuses over $1M and the silent blank-field defaults are where the job goes wrong.
evidence.domain: Compared with IRS Pub 15 (2026) section 7 and SSA's 2026 wage base $184,500 (default matches). Correct: SS cap against YTD, Medicare uncapped, Additional Medicare withheld on wages over $200,000 regardless of filing status, no employer match on it, 401(k) deferrals subject to FICA, gross-up formula net/(1-sum). Departures: (1) no mandatory 37% supplemental rate above $1M of supplemental wages in the year (a CPP would flag this first for any exec bonus); (2) settlement uses one flat marginal rate and ignores Additional Medicare reconciliation thresholds by filing status ($250k MFJ), acceptable as a stated estimate; (3) no state supplemental-rate guidance beyond 'some states have their own', so a user in a state with a fixed supplemental rate must find it alone.

defects.what: No mandatory 37% federal withholding on supplemental wages over $1,000,000 in the year (Pub 15 sec 7). A $1.5M bonus at the labelled 22% withholds 330,000 instead of 405,000, overstating take-home by $75,000; gross-ups above $1M are understated (1,415,428 vs 1,527,403 for $1M net at YTD $200k of regular wages; corrected by the round lead from 1,581,312, which assumed the YTD wages were supplemental).
Blank or unparsable fields silently fall back to the example defaults and the box is refilled: a cleared 'Wages already paid' runs at $90,000, a cleared state rate at 5%.

grossUp returns 6.43e64 (shown as a dollar amount) when no gross can reach the target (100% deferral, or withholding rates summing to 100% or more); the comment claims net is monotonic increasing everywhere.
Field label and meta description present 22% as 'the flat supplemental rate' with no $1M / 37% caveat; the 'Not decided' and README Limits lists omit it.
Dropping Additional Medicare from the after-tax value survives the tests; no test covers bonuses over $1M or an unsolvable gross-up.
Negative rates or amounts are silently clipped to 0 by nz() instead of rejected.

verdict: For an ordinary bonus the arithmetic is exact: the default example (net 6,535, employer cost 10,765), the $10,000 net gross-up (15,302.22), the gross-up across the 2026 Social Security base (14,366.18) and the Additional Medicare line at $195k YTD all reproduce from Pub 15 and SSA figures, the 2026 wage base default is right, 401(k) deferrals correctly stay in FICA, and 25 tests catch 4 of 5 seeded mutants. It misses the bar on correctness, claims and domain: the tool has no mandatory 37% supplemental rate over $1M, so the exact executive and large gross-up cases a payroll specialist checks first are wrong by tens of thousands of dollars while the page calls 22% 'the flat supplemental rate'; an unsolvable gross-up prints 6.4e64 dollars; and blank fields silently run at the example's values.
